summaries.summary: Human language comprehension involves partially identified cognitive processes, with EEG and ERPs used to study meaning integration across words.
Six ERP components from BIBREF0 are analyzed, and a pretrained language model is proposed to probe language features driving ERPs and comprehension.
ERP components are baseline-relative electrical responses named by polarity, timing, and scalp distribution, with N400, P600, PNP, EPNP, LAN, and ELAN introduced.
Prior work links surprisal, distance, LSTM, RNNG, and recurrent neural networks to ERPs or MEG, while this work directly predicts ERPs without a linking function.
All six ERP components from BIBREF0 are predicted above chance by a pretrained language model, including P600 prediction from an LSTM unlike BIBREF7.
Multitask learning shows shared information among ERP components and behavioral data, potentially clarifying ERP drivers and human language comprehension processes.
ERP components are predicted from fine-tuned language models, multitask learning reveals expected and surprising relationships, and heterogeneous data sharing may benefit small datasets.
The authors thank reviewers and acknowledge support in part by National Institutes of Health grant number U01NS098969.
Appendix visualizations and supplemental multitask variants show bi-LSTM superiority, qualitatively similar relationships, and Pearson correlations differing from joint-training benefit patterns.
